title: Soft day, your honour!
html_source: Soft day is Irish slang, meaning ‘wet’ or ‘dreary’ day.

anchor.prefix:
to Dublin from the Ards of Down to do so. 

1939#25

Lal the ral the ra 
The rocky road to Dublin. 

1922#31

 A gruff squire on horseback with shiny topboots. Soft day, sir John!
anchor.suffix:
... Day!... Day!... Two topboots jog dangling on to Dublin. Lal the ral the ra. Lal the ral the raddy. 

1932#29

 — That reminds me, Mr Deasy said. You can do me a favour, 1961#31
